filled.description:
Whether or not this specific instance has been processed. Especially helpful when calls from the
front end require full resolution and serves as a marker for server to know entire instance has
been fully resolved.

id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

query.description:
PromQL query in the syntax of https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/querying/basics/

{@link #query} can be parameterized in the format of {@link Template}. There should be no hardcoded metric names in the query, they
must all be parameterized via {@link App.Meter}s.

References to {@link App.Meter} -
1. "Static" - must be parameterized via `meters` variable name (as a reference to {@link App.Metric#meters}) and use
   array syntax to reference index.
   Ex: `${meters[0]}{directory="/tmp"}` will resolve to the first {@link App.Metric.MeterRef} in {@link #meters} and ultimately be replaced
         with the {@link App.Metric.MeterRef#meter} name as known by the underlying {@link App.MeterRegistry}.
2. "Dynamic" - must be parameterized via {@link App.Metric#APP_METER_DYNAMIC_REFERENCE} value, `meters_d`, and use
   array syntax to reference index.
   The value supplied at runtime must be an array of {@link App.Metric.MeterRef}s.
   Ex: `sum(${meters_d[0]}{tag1="bar"}) by (tag1)` with `variables: { meters_d: [{meter: "my_app_meter"}] }` will resolve to the
        metric name of as known by the underlying {@link App.MeterRegistry} during runtime.

References to {@link App.Metric} -
1. "Static" - must be parameterized via `metrics` variable name (as a reference to {@link App.Metric#metrics}) and use
   array syntax to reference index. Variables defined in a static parameterized reference must be supplied in its parent metric's
   {@link App.Metric.QuerySpec#variables}.
   Ex: `${metrics[0]} * 100` will resolve to the first {@link App.Metric} in {@link #metrics} and ultimately be replaced with the
       resolved {@link App.Metric#query} of `metrics[0]`.
1. "Dynamic" - must be parameterized via {@link App.Metric#APP_METRIC_DYNAMIC_REFERENCE} value, `metrics_d`, and use
   array syntax to reference index.
   The value supplied at runtime must be an array of {@link App.Metric.Bound<App.Metric.QuerySpec>}s.
   Ex: `(${metrics_d[0]} / ${metrics_d[1]}) * 100`. with
       `variables: { metrics_d: [
         { type: 'App.Metric.Bound<App.Metric.QuerySpec>', metric: 'jvm-memory-usage'},
         { type: 'App.Metric.Bound<App.Metric.QuerySpec>', metric: 'container-memory-limits'}
        ]}`
        will give jvm usage as a percent of limits.

References to {@link App.Metric.Variable} -
1. must be parameterized via `variables` variable name (as a reference to {@link App.Metric#variables}) and use
   array syntax to reference index. Values can be supplied at runtime via {@link App.Metric.QuerySpec#variables}
   in which the referenced {@link App.Metric.Variable#id} is the key.
   Ex: `{$meters[0]}{foo="${variables[0]}", bar="fire"}`

unit.description: The unit to set on the returned timeseries in {@link #evaluate}'s {@link EvalMetricsResult}.

meters.description:
Static {@link App.Meter} references that are bound to this metric.
@see #query

metrics.description:
Static {@link App.Metric} references that are are bound to this metric.
@see #query

variables.description:
List of variables that can be used to alter the evaluation of the {@link App.Metric}.
@see #query

return.description: Supported return scopes for the metric

sourceTemplate.description:
Template for how to compose unique source ids for the {@link EvalMetricResult} (ie the keys of {@link EvalMetricResult#result} map).
Encoding default values in the template is not supported. Template variable names must be {@link App.Meter} tags names
that are returned from the metric query results.
If not specified, the source id will be the index of the returned series.
If specified poorly the system will still return data but populate {@link EvalMetricsResult#errors} with details. For example,
if the sourceTemplate cannot be resolved (ie the Template has variables that are not present in the tags) or if the sourceTemplate
does not generate unique ids for each series returned.

title: Abstraction over any timeseries based metric for a specific {@link App} or {@link Env}.
name: App.Metric
